Reference / http/routing

http/routing#

Routing: patterns, routes and a table that picks the handler.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let app = Routes(
    routes: [
        Route(method: Method.get, pattern: RoutePattern("/users/:id"), handling: ShowUser()),
        Route(method: Method.get, pattern: RoutePattern("/files/*path"), handling: Files()),
        Route(pattern: RoutePattern("/health"), handling: Health()),          // every method
    ],
    fallback: NotFound(),
);
// in ShowUser: context.parameters()["id"]

Description#

Routing: patterns, routes and a table that picks the handler.

:name takes one path segment and *name the rest of the path (last only); segments are matched decoded. The most specific pattern wins, and on one pattern the route of the request's own method wins over an any-method one. A path no pattern matches goes to the fallback; a matching path with the wrong method is answered 405 with Allow. web/routing builds on this.

object Routes#

object Routes does Handling

A route table, and the Handling that sends each request to its route.

Patterns of one method may overlap: a request goes to the most specific one (#103). Segment by segment, left to right, a literal wins over a parameter and a parameter over a final wildcard; a pattern that ends with the path wins over a wildcard that would take nothing:

GET /users/me       before  GET /users/:id
GET /files/index    before  GET /files/*path
GET /files          before  GET /files/*path

When the most specific pattern has no route for the method, the next one is tried: with POST /users/me and GET /users/:id, GET /users/me reaches /users/:id. Within one pattern the method's own route wins, and HEAD falls back to GET. Only two routes of one method with the same shape, such as /users/:id and /users/:name, are refused, at construction.

The table becomes a segment tree on the first request, so finding the route takes one step per path segment, whatever the number of routes (#104).

Routes.Routes#

Routes(routes is Sequencing<Route>, fallback is Handling)

The table, with empty 400 and 405 answers; InvalidRoute for two routes of one method and shape.

Routes.Routes#

Routes(routes is Sequencing<Route>, fallback is Handling, rejection is RouteRejecting, slashes is SlashPolicy = SlashPolicy.strict)

slashes: SlashPolicy.redirect answers a path no route matches with 308 to the same path with or without its final slash, when that one matches (#105); strict, the default, sends it to the fallback.
